CHIEF COMPLAINT
Pain at the end of right middle finger.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient is a 41-year-old female who sustained a motor vehicle accident approximately four to five days ago. She was stopped at a four-way stop when a vehicle behind her rear-ended her. The patient became angry and extended her middle finger in response, striking the ceiling of the car. She has had right middle finger pain since the incident. X-ray shows a distal phalanx fracture of the right middle finger. Physical examination reveals tenderness over the distal phalanx of the right middle finger with reproduction of pain on palpation over that area. No other injuries from the accident.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Not discussed.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Atrial fibrillation.

MEDICATIONS
Digoxin.

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Motor vehicle accident four to five days ago from being rear-ended at a four-way stop.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Tenderness over distal phalanx of right middle finger. Pain reproduced with palpation over the distal phalanx. No tenderness noted distally. Otherwise normal examination.

RESULTS
X-ray of right middle finger shows distal phalanx fracture.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Distal phalanx fracture of the right middle finger. Patient prescribed tramadol 50 mg every six hours as needed for pain, eight tablets dispensed for two days. Placed in finger splint. Follow-up x-ray in two weeks.
